fm_paparazzi_lunch.text: A man in a bush photographs your salad. He appears to have been in the bush since breakfast.

outcomes.flattering: The photo runs under 'Radiant and Carb-Aware'. You look wonderful, and the bush is thrilled.
outcomes.unflattering: You are caught mid-chew. The headline reads 'Is This Decline?'

fm_talk_show_interview.text: A late-night host offers you the couch and ten minutes of rehearsed spontaneity.

outcomes.hit: You land every joke. The host laughs at the right moments, which is his job.
outcomes.flop: Your anecdote has no ending. The audience applauds anyway, out of pity.

fm_award_nomination.text: You are nominated for an award with a golden object and a very long speech time limit.

outcomes.win: They say your name. You thank everyone, including a dentist.
outcomes.lose: You lose to someone you know. You clap with the intensity of a hostage.

fm_stalker.text: The same person has been outside your gate for nine days. They have started bringing a folding chair.

outcomes.resolved: The authorities remove the chair, and eventually the person. You sleep with the lights on anyway.
outcomes.escalates: It gets worse before it gets better. You hire security with a very small mustache.

fm_endorsement_soda.text: A beverage company offers a lot of money for your face next to a drink you have never tasted.

outcomes.richer: Your agent says the word 'exclusivity' and the number doubles. Everyone leaves tired and happy.
outcomes.walks: The company finds a younger face for the same bubbles. You are told this is just business.

fm_social_storm.text: A joke you posted at 3 a.m. has been reread by several million strangers in the worst possible tone.

outcomes.forgiven: The apology is accepted by lunch and mocked by dinner. Net loss, but tolerable.
outcomes.worse: The apology is called 'not an apology'. A second apology is called 'a hostage video'.

fm_tell_all_book.text: A publisher offers you a fortune for a tell-all memoir. They would like names, dates and at least one 'incident'.

fm_charity_gala.text: A charity gala has a plate of food that costs one thousand dollars, and a speech about hunger.

outcomes.noticed: A photographer catches the check. For once the camera is useful.
outcomes.quiet: No one notices. Somewhere, a small amount of good happens anyway.

fm_fan_encounter.text: A fan stops you on the street, shaking, holding a tattered photo of your face.

outcomes.lovely: They cry a little. You feel like a landmark, but a pleasant one.
outcomes.viral: Your blinking face becomes a meme titled 'Dead Inside'. You have never felt more seen.

fm_comeback.text: Your career has been quiet for a while. A producer calls with the word 'comeback' and the phrase 'low budget'.

outcomes.triumph: Critics call it a return to form. You did not know you had left a form.
outcomes.flop: The film opens on a Tuesday to an empty hall and a cleaner.

fm_aging_role.text: The roles on offer are now 'Grandfather' and 'Wise Old Mentor'. You stare at the script like it owes you money.

outcomes.won: The director blinks first. You get the lead, plus a lighting crew who adore you.
outcomes.lost: You are told you are 'a bit much'. The mentor role goes to someone else.

fm_leaked_photo.text: A photo of you at your most human has been published. It involves a pastry and no pants.

outcomes.removed: The photo vanishes from the major sites and spreads quietly through the minor ones.
outcomes.streisand: Your lawyers have made the photo more famous. It now has its own fan page.

fm_fan_mail.text: A sack of fan mail arrives. One envelope contains a drawing of you, a marriage proposal and a lock of unknown hair.

outcomes.delight: The fan will tell this story at every party for forty years.
outcomes.trouble: The fan announces the reply on every platform. Others are now owed letters.

fm_reality_offer.text: A network wants to film your daily life. Your daily life consists of waiting, mostly, but they say they will edit it.

outcomes.ratings: The show is a hit. A random cousin becomes famous for no reason, which is the genre.
outcomes.canceled: It is canceled after four episodes. You were cast as 'The Difficult One'.

fm_agent_dumps.text: Your agent calls to say that 'it isn't a fit anymore'. He is already representing the person you were compared to.

outcomes.stays: He agrees to stay, citing your 'potential', which is how people describe a leaky boat.
outcomes.no: He pretends the line has gone dead. Then he pretends it for a while.

fm_viral_clip.text: A clip of you tripping over a red carpet is going around the world. You are aerodynamic in it.

outcomes.jackpot: The parody does better than your work. You decide not to think about that.
outcomes.cringe: The parody is called 'trying too hard'. They are not wrong.

fm_signing_autographs.text: A line of two thousand people wants their copy signed. Your hand has already filed a complaint.

fm_rival_feud.text: A colleague has told a magazine that you are 'the opposite of talent, in a nice jacket'. Your phone is lit up like a bonfire.

outcomes.won: Your reply is brutal, precise and, you notice, funnier than their whole career.
outcomes.lost: Their reply is funnier. You are, for the first time, relieved no one reads.

fm_first_audition.text: You stand in a corridor with forty people who look exactly like you. A woman with a clipboard calls your name incorrectly.

outcomes.booked: You get the part. The woman with the clipboard learns your name.
outcomes.next: You do not get it. You get a sandwich, which is not nothing.

fm_street_recognition.text: A stranger says, 'Aren't you somebody?' You say yes. They look let down.

outcomes.fun: A small crowd gathers and takes pictures. You are a tourist attraction now.
outcomes.awkward: The stranger says, 'Actually, I meant the other somebody.' Nobody speaks for a while.

fm_cel_perfume.text: A fragrance house wants your name on a bottle. The scent will be called 'You', and will smell of regret and bergamot.

outcomes.masterpiece: You pick a smell by accident. It sells out in an afternoon.
outcomes.disaster: It smells faintly of wet carpet. Critics call it 'bold'.

fm_cel_biopic.text: Producers want to make a film about your life. They say you will be played by 'someone attractive' and 'much taller'.

outcomes.acclaimed: The film is beloved. Your character cries at a piano, which you do not remember doing.
outcomes.embarrassing: The film is accurate in all the ways that hurt. They kept the pastry.

fm_cel_hall_of_fame.text: You are invited to join a hall of fame. It is a building, and has recently added a wing for you.

outcomes.legend: The room roars. A donor chokes on a canape, in a respectful way.
outcomes.gaffe: You say something about the chairman's wig. The chairman is not wearing a wig.

fm_cel_fan_riot.text: You announce a surprise appearance for fans. Nine thousand arrive, in a space meant for four hundred.

outcomes.heroic: You speak softly and everyone sits down. It is the closest thing to magic you have done.
outcomes.chaos: You are carried briefly by the crowd and returned without a shoe.

fm_cel_fake_death_rumor.text: A website announces your death. You find out by reading your own tribute, which is mostly positive.

outcomes.comedy: Your reply is the funniest thing you have posted. Mourners return as fans.
outcomes.flat: No one notices you are alive. The tribute is still trending.

fm_cel_paparazzi_helicopter.text: A helicopter hovers over your garden. It carries two photographers and, somehow, a drone with lenses.

outcomes.win: A judge awards you damages and a stern letter to the helicopter.
outcomes.lose: The judge points out that sky is public. You pay for the privilege of being told so.

fm_cel_statue.text: A city wants to unveil a statue of you. The sculptor has been told to be generous around the middle.

outcomes.iconic: The statue and you appear in postcards. The statue looks less tired.
outcomes.pigeon: A pigeon lands on the statue's head at the exact moment of the photo. It becomes the postcard.

fm_cel_political_run.text: A party suggests you run for office. Your qualifications are your face and a high approval rating among strangers.

outcomes.elected: You win, mostly on name recognition. Governing, you learn, involves more paperwork than glamour.
outcomes.lost: You lose by a margin so wide a pollster sends flowers.

fm_cel_retire_early.text: You are exhausted by being a brand. Your manager says retirement is 'a bold move, creatively and financially'.

outcomes.peace: You grow tomatoes. Nobody asks what you think about anything.
outcomes.bored: By autumn you have drafted three comebacks and sent none of them.

fm_cel_roast.text: You are invited to be roasted on stage by your closest friends. They have been taking notes for years.

outcomes.beloved: You laugh at your own flaws. The audience likes you more, which is suspicious.
outcomes.wounded: One joke is too accurate. You smile until you are in the car.

ry_tutor_etiquette.text: Your etiquette tutor spends six hours teaching you which fork to use. Neither of you has ever used one.

outcomes.charming: The tutor is horrified, then writes it down as 'brilliantly eccentric'.
outcomes.scolded: You are sent to your chambers, which are bigger than most houses.

ry_school_press.text: Photographers wait outside your school gates, each with a lens longer than your arm.

outcomes.adored: The face goes on a mug. Your parents say nothing, loudly.
outcomes.scandal: Editorials ask what is wrong with the youth. You are twelve.

ry_portrait_sitting.text: A painter wants you to sit still for four hours so you will look noble. You cannot feel your legs.

outcomes.quirky: The finished portrait captures a blur. It is declared 'daring' and hung in the hall.
outcomes.ruined: The painter sighs for forty minutes and hangs it in a closet.

ry_secret_passage.text: You find a hidden passage behind the library. It smells of dust, secrets and at least one old sandwich.

outcomes.treasure: You find a chest of old jewels the crown forgot. You give most of it back.
outcomes.lost: You wander for hours. Guards find you in the pantry, and everyone pretends it never happened.

ry_childhood_parade.text: You must ride in a golden carriage and wave at crowds for three hours. The carriage has no suspension.

outcomes.unseen: No one sees. Crumbs fall in places even the royal cleaner will not find.
outcomes.caught: A camera catches you mid-bite. The caption is unkind to the pie.

ry_palace_gossip.text: The palace staff are whispering about you. Not unkindly, just constantly, and in alphabetical order.

outcomes.useful: You learn two secrets and a better way to the kitchens.
outcomes.backfire: You hear something about yourself that is true. This is worse.

ry_ribbon_cutting.text: You are asked to open a bridge, a hospital and a small cheese factory. Scissors are provided.

outcomes.moving: People cry in a good way. A nurse hands you a biscuit.
outcomes.gaffe: You call the hospital by the wrong name. The headline writes itself.

ry_commoner_romance.text: You fall for someone who has never owned a tiara and finds the whole thing funny. The court finds it less so.

outcomes.blessed: The nation loves a love story. The court acts surprised, then pleased, then relieved.
outcomes.scandal: The papers print 'Palace in Turmoil' over your photo. The commoner proposes anyway.

ry_tabloid_scandal.text: A tabloid claims you have been seen at a questionable club with a person of questionable cheekbones.

outcomes.believed: The palace statement uses the word 'categorically'. It works for a week.
outcomes.exposed: A photo of you in sunglasses at 4 a.m. appears and contradicts the word 'categorically'.

ry_coup_rumor.text: A guard whispers that some lords are planning a coup. He is nervous, and also holding your coat.

outcomes.foiled: You spot the plot in time and with fine timing. The lords are retired to the countryside.
outcomes.trapped: The plot was real, and you were not invited. You leave the country at dawn.

ry_state_dinner.text: A foreign dignitary sits beside you at a state dinner and says nothing for six courses.

outcomes.friend: You discover a mutual love of competitive gardening. A treaty feels imminent.
outcomes.faux_pas: You ask about a war the dignitary lost. Dessert is served in silence.

ry_arranged_match.text: The court has arranged a marriage to a prince or princess with excellent borders and a mild personality.

outcomes.fond: You are surprised to like them. The borders are lovely too.
outcomes.cold: The marriage is stable and dull as a ledger. Your portraits look very good together.

ry_royal_tour.text: You must tour six regions in nine days, shake four thousand hands and be photographed with a goat.

outcomes.viral: The goat nuzzles you and the crowd melts. A fan club for the goat is founded.
outcomes.bitten: The goat has opinions. The photographers love it too much.

ry_charity_patronage.text: A good cause asks you to be its patron. This requires one appearance a year and a sincere face.

outcomes.praised: You bring attention to something that needed it. A few sneer; most thank you.
outcomes.backlash: Half the realm cheers, the other half writes letters in capital letters.

ry_inheritance_squabble.text: Your siblings are fighting over a castle. It is drafty, haunted and very desirable.

outcomes.win: You win the castle. The haunting is included at no extra cost.
outcomes.lose: Your sibling gets the castle, and keeps the ghost, who prefers them.

ry_royal_wedding_guest.text: You are seated at a cousin's wedding between a duke who whispers and a countess who hums. The cake is eleven tiers of obligation.

outcomes.lovely: Your toast is short, warm and only slightly flammable. The couple weep, kindly.
outcomes.blunder: You use the wrong name for the groom. He answers to it for the rest of the evening.

ry_sign_tax_law.text: Your council presents a new tax on candles, because apparently the kingdom is running low on money and light.

outcomes.smart: The council reworks it into a luxury tax on chandeliers. Nobody cries for chandeliers.
outcomes.stall: The council takes six months to forget they were angry. Candles remain taxed.

ry_sign_holiday_law.text: A bill proposes a national holiday in your honour. It is to be called 'Appreciation Day' and to feature a parade.

outcomes.admired: The press calls you humble. The parade goes ahead anyway under a different name.
outcomes.ungrateful: People had planned costumes. You cannot unplan costumes.

ry_execute_order.text: A convicted traitor awaits your signature. The law allows execution. Your conscience has asked to be excused from the room.

outcomes.merciful: They leave by night. The people say you are fair and, privately, a bit soft.
outcomes.returns: They return in a year with an army of thirteen. The council is not pleased.

ry_abdication_pressure.text: Advisors, relatives and one cheeky bishop suggest the throne might be better off with someone younger. You are not sure who they mean.

outcomes.steady: You remain monarch. The bishop learns to like you, or at least how to hide it.
outcomes.crisis: The press smells blood. You smell soup, and nothing else is going well.

ry_succession.text: Your parent, the monarch, has died. The court looks at you the way a nervous waiter looks at a final tip.

outcomes.respected: The nation sees a ruler who feels. The ministers see a ruler who is slow.
outcomes.vacuum: Rivals use your grief to tidy up the paperwork. You get rid of three of them later.

ry_budget_crisis.text: The treasury is empty. The treasurer shows you the ledger, then shows you a second ledger, and you decide to sit down.

outcomes.stable: The books balance. The crowds are unhappy, but ready for soup.
outcomes.riot: Austerity is badly received. A bread riot begins outside the palace gate.

ry_peasant_petition.text: A commoner presents a petition about a pothole. It is, to be fair, a very large pothole.

outcomes.beloved: You pose beside the pothole. Soon it is a landmark and a small tourist boom.
outcomes.fall: You fall into the pothole in front of a hundred witnesses. It is fixed within the week.

ry_war_council.text: A neighbouring kingdom has insulted your hat. The generals are ready, and the generals are keen.

outcomes.victory: A short, noisy victory. Hat sales surge.
outcomes.defeat: The war is long, expensive and mostly muddy. The hat is lost.

ry_jubilee.text: The kingdom plans a jubilee for your reign. There will be flags, fireworks and a small orchestra of unwilling relatives.

outcomes.tears: The crowd weeps. A fireworks technician weeps and also lights something early.
outcomes.mumble: You lose your place and read the speech a second time. Everyone cheers anyway.
